events.title: Byah Haath
events.ritualDescription: A Marwari pre-wedding ritual in which the groom's family formally commences wedding preparations. Sacred items are arranged and elders offer prayers to mark the official start of the wedding celebrations.

events.title: Aibhuro Bhaat
events.ritualDescription: A beloved Bengali ritual celebrating the bride's last meal as an unmarried woman. Family and friends gather to feed her with love, sing songs, and cherish this tender farewell to her life before marriage.

events.title: Ganesh Pujan
events.ritualDescription: The groom's family gathers to seek the blessings of Lord Ganesha, remover of obstacles and bestower of auspicious beginnings, before the wedding festivities begin in earnest.

events.title: Haldi
events.ritualDescription: A joyful Marwari ritual where turmeric paste is applied to the groom by close family and friends, purifying the body and spirit, and giving him a radiant glow before the wedding.

events.title: Mehendi
events.ritualDescription: Henna is applied to the groom's hands as a symbol of good luck and the beauty of new beginnings. Close relatives celebrate around him with music and laughter.

events.title: Rati Jaga
events.ritualDescription: A vibrant Marwari night vigil where women of the family stay awake singing traditional folk songs, keeping the festive energy alive through the night before the wedding.

events.title: Mehendi
events.ritualDescription: Intricate henna designs are applied to the bride's hands and feet by a mehendi artist, surrounded by close family and friends. The darker the mehendi, the deeper the love — a beloved pre-wedding tradition.

events.title: Chaak Bhaat Mayra
events.ritualDescription: A significant Marwari pre-wedding ritual in which the groom's maternal uncle arrives with an abundance of gifts and sweets for the family, symbolizing maternal love, generosity, and blessings.

events.title: Tilak / Engagement
events.ritualDescription: The formal engagement ceremony where the bride's family applies tilak to the groom, symbolising acceptance and the sealing of the union between both families.

events.title: Sangeet
events.ritualDescription: An evening of song, dance, and joy as both families perform choreographed numbers blending Rajasthani and Bengali folk traditions, celebrating the couple with food, music, and shared memories.

events.title: Haldi / Gaye Holud / Carnival & Lunch
events.ritualDescription: A vibrant fusion celebration combining the Marwari Haldi ceremony and Bengali Gaye Holud, set in a festive carnival atmosphere. Both families apply turmeric to the couple, and everyone enjoys a shared lunch steeped in colour and joy.

events.title: Sehrabandhi
events.ritualDescription: Elders ceremonially tie the groom's floral sehra over his face before he departs for the wedding, blessing him with strength, dignity, and happiness.

events.title: Baarat
events.ritualDescription: The groom's joyful wedding procession arrives with a dhol, dancing guests, and festive energy — celebrating his arrival and the beginning of the wedding ceremony.

events.title: Samela
events.ritualDescription: The groom is formally received by the bride's family at the venue entrance, with warm greetings and blessings exchanged between the elders of both families.

events.title: Bor Baran / Toran / Groom Entry
events.ritualDescription: The groom formally enters the wedding venue. The bride's mother performs the Bengali borun ritual, welcoming him with sacred items, while toran leaves adorning the entrance ward off evil and invite prosperity.

events.title: Bride Entry
events.ritualDescription: The bride makes her grand entrance, traditionally carrying betel leaves to shield her face — a graceful and emotional Bengali custom as she is escorted to the mandap by her brothers.

events.title: Varmala / Mala Bodol
events.ritualDescription: Rahul and Shinjini exchange floral garlands in a playful and joyful ceremony — a fusion of the Marwari varmala and Bengali mala bodol — symbolising their heartfelt acceptance of each other.

events.title: Phere
events.ritualDescription: The couple circles the sacred fire seven times, each round a solemn vow of love, loyalty, and companionship, witnessed by family, gods, and the eternal flame.

events.title: Bidai
events.ritualDescription: One of the most emotional moments of a Bengali wedding — Shinjini bids farewell to her family as she leaves for her new home, throwing back handfuls of puffed rice as a final offering and blessing.

events.title: Reception & Dinner
events.ritualDescription: An evening reception where family and friends celebrate Rahul and Shinjini as a married couple with dinner, blessings, and a joyful send-off into their new life together.
